=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of the Seller's Update and Disclosure Letter

## Preliminary point: the "[STANDARD]" labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's package marks most clauses "[STANDARD]". It says these have been "reviewed and cleared by both sides", that only "[OPEN]" items need scrutiny, and that "the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package."

**I have not relied on this.**
- No clause in the package is actually marked [OPEN].
- Nothing in the documents shows that Wattlebridge agreed to any of these positions.
- The Seller's own covering email asks for our mark-up, which is inconsistent with the positions being agreed.
- The Disclosure Letter (clause 11) itself says the Buyer "must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement."

I have reviewed every clause. Several "[STANDARD]" items are the most buyer-adverse in the package.

**Recommendation:** State in our response that no position is agreed until the Buyer confirms it in writing. If anyone on our side has informally agreed any of these points, please let me know.

---

## A. Limitation regime

### 1. Fundamental warranties subject to the general cap and time limit (Title/Capacity)
**Seller position:** Title and capacity warranties sit under the 20% cap (AUD 4.8m) and the 18-month time limit, "for administrative simplicity."

**Why it hurts us:** Title is what we are paying AUD 24m for. If the Seller does not own 100% of the shares free of encumbrances, our loss could be the full price, but recovery would be capped at AUD 4.8m. This position is well off market.

**Push back:**
- Cap fundamental warranties at 100% of the price.
- No de minimis or basket for fundamental warranties.
- Time limit of at least 6 years, or the statutory limitation period.

### 2. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
**Why it hurts us:**
- As drafted, the limitations would arguably extend to fraud, specific indemnities, tax claims, leakage and completion-mechanic claims.
- Clause 12.3 makes this the default: all limitations apply to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise."

**Push back:**
- Reverse the default so limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.
- Carve out the following expressly:
  - fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment by the Seller or its agents (no cap or time limit);
  - fundamental warranties (see item 1);
  - the tax indemnity and tax warranties;
  - specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006 incident, bonuses, Riverlark);
  - leakage and price-adjustment claims.
- Non-reliance should not exclude fraud. It should also be tested against the Australian Consumer Law s18 (misleading or deceptive conduct) exposure, where contractual exclusions have limited effect.

### 3. General cap of 20% and thresholds (cl 12.1 / 12.2)
**Analysis:**
- The 20% cap is within the negotiable range for general warranties. Whether to accept it depends on whether we take out warranty and indemnity (W&I) insurance.
- The de minimis (AUD 25k, about 0.1% of price) and basket (AUD 250k, about 1% of price) are within market range.
- The basket is drafted as **excess only**. If total claims reach AUD 250k, the Seller pays nothing; if they reach AUD 300k, it pays AUD 50k.

**Push back:**
- A **tipping basket**: once the threshold is met, the Seller pays from the first dollar.
- Related claims count together toward the de minimis.
- A cap of 30–50% if there is no W&I insurance.

### 4. Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13)
**Analysis:** 18 months is broadly acceptable for general warranties. It is inadequate for tax, because the ATO amendment period for companies is generally 4 years and unlimited for fraud or evasion.

**Push back:**
- Tax: 5–7 years, or the amendment period plus 6 months.
- Fundamental warranties: as in item 1.
- Specific indemnities: until the underlying matter is finally resolved.

### 5. "Tax / IP positions settled under the general regime"
**Push back:** These are not settled. We need:
- a standalone tax indemnity covering pre-Completion periods, including payroll tax and superannuation on the bonuses (item 9);
- IP warranties treated outside the general cap, at least for the Ironquay issue.

### 6. Recovery risk: the Seller is a venture vehicle
Harbourglass Ventures may distribute the sale proceeds soon after Completion. An uncapped indemnity is of little value against an empty shell.

**Push back:** One of:
- an escrow or retention, for example AUD 2–2.4m for 18 months plus a specific amount for the DD-006 incident;
- a parent or fund guarantee;
- W&I insurance, together with retained specific indemnities for known issues, which W&I insurers exclude.

---

## B. Disclosure and Buyer knowledge

### 7. General disclosure of the whole data room and public registers (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2; Schedule 7)
**Why it hurts us:** Every fact anywhere in the data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers or "publicly searchable corporate records" would qualify every warranty. The warranties would be close to worthless.

**Push back:**
- Only specific disclosures count, and only if fairly disclosed with enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its effect.
- No general disclosure of the data room. At most, the data room index is deemed disclosed and no more.
- Public records limited to searches of named registers conducted on a stated date.
- Disclosure never qualifies fundamental warranties, the tax indemnity or the specific indemnities.
- The data room cut-off is 22 September 2026, which is now about six weeks old. Any updated disclosure at the warranty bring-down must not cure breaches. Instead, it should give us a walk right or a claim.

### 8. Buyer knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3)
**Why it hurts us:** The clause bars any claim about matters known to the Buyer "or its advisers", **including anything "discoverable"** from the data room or public records. This is an anti-sandbagging clause based on constructive knowledge. Combined with item 7, it is a second route that removes warranty protection.

**Push back, in order of preference:**
1. Delete the clause and state that the Buyer's knowledge does not affect its claims.
2. Fallback: exclude only matters within the *actual* knowledge of named Buyer deal-team individuals, and only to the extent fairly disclosed.
3. In either case, no imputation of advisers' knowledge.

---

## C. Deal-specific issues

On several points the Disclosure Letter contradicts the Seller's Update.

### 9. Employee Completion bonuses, AUD 420,000 (DD-005)
**What the documents show:**
- The Seller Update says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow.
- The Disclosure Letter (item 5) confirms they are not in the funds flow and does not say whether on-costs apply.
- If the Company pays them, the Buyer bears the cost economically. That is a value transfer on a debt-free/cash-free deal.
- The AUD 420k exposure grows once on-costs are added: NSW payroll tax, possibly superannuation depending on the bonus terms, and PAYG withholding administration.

**Push back:**
- Treat the bonuses plus all on-costs as **Indebtedness or Transaction Costs**, deducted from the price in the funds flow. Alternatively, the Seller pays them directly at Completion.
- Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall, outside the cap and thresholds.

### 10. Riverlark facility, about AUD 3.2m (DD-003)
**What the documents show:**
- The Seller proposes a release "following Completion."
- The Disclosure Letter (item 3) confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge exists.
- The facility contains a change-control clause (8.1). Completion without repayment could trigger a default against the Company we will then own.
- The security may extend to the shares themselves, which would also go to title.

**Push back:** Repayment **at Completion** is non-negotiable on a debt-free/cash-free basis. Completion deliverables should include:
- a payoff letter;
- an executed deed of release;
- PPSR financing change statements, or an undertaking to lodge them within a short fixed period;
- release of any share security.

The repayment amount should be paid from the price directly to Riverlark. We also need warranty confirmation that no other security exists.

### 11. Bluefen consent: about 30% of revenue, AUD 3.6m (DD-002)
**What the documents show:**
- The Seller says the consent is "addressed", but the Disclosure Letter (item 2) says there is no final consent and no evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- "Reasonable endeavours", plus deemed satisfaction on delivery of *any* written consent, would let a consent with onerous conditions satisfy the condition. Examples would be repricing or a shortened term.

**Push back:**
- Make it a condition precedent: unconditional written consent from Bluefen, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer acting reasonably. All 11.3 conditions must be satisfied or be on terms the Buyer accepts.
- The Seller should use "all reasonable endeavours", with the Buyer involved in communications with Bluefen.
- The condition is waivable only by the Buyer, with a long-stop date and a termination right.
- Add a warranty that Bluefen has not indicated it will terminate, reduce or renegotiate.

### 12. Ironquay SOW3 IP (DD-004 / DD-010)
**What the documents show:**
- Clause 7.3 means the SOW3 Project Materials **do not transfer** until all SOW3 fees are paid.
- AUD 180,000 is recorded as open. There is no evidence of payment and no confirmatory assignment.
- The existing indemnity covers only the payment. It does not cover:
  - losing the IP;
  - third-party infringement claims;
  - redevelopment or replacement costs;
  - business interruption.

**Push back:**
- Before Completion, either pay Ironquay out, with the payment treated as a debt-like deduction if made by the Company, or obtain an executed **confirmatory assignment** from Ironquay. Make this a condition precedent or Completion deliverable.
- Broaden the specific indemnity to cover all loss from any failure of the Company to own the SOW3 materials. It should sit outside the general cap and thresholds and not be qualified by disclosure.

### 13. DD-006 export and privacy incident (about 1,240 records)
**What the documents show:**
- The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." The Disclosure Letter says scope, access and notification status are all unknown.
- The data includes names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps, which is personal information.
- Under the Privacy Act's Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity must reasonably and expeditiously assess a suspected eligible data breach, generally within 30 days of becoming aware.
- The incident predates 22 September 2026, so that period has likely passed. A failure to assess or notify may already be a compliance issue in its own right.
- Privacy penalties and regulator scrutiny have increased materially since the 2022 amendments.

**Push back:**
- Require immediate disclosure of:
  - the full incident file;
  - the date of awareness;
  - the steps taken;
  - any forensic report;
  - any OAIC or affected-individual notification.
- Add a pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment, make any required notifications and keep the Buyer informed.
- Add a **specific indemnity** for all loss from the incident (regulator penalties, claims, remediation and notification costs). It should sit outside the cap, basket and de minimis, not be qualified by disclosure, and be backed by escrow.
- Consider a condition or walk right if the investigation reveals a materially larger incident.

### 14. Sandbar supplier renewals, 3 × AUD 110,000 (DD-008 / DD-011)
**What the documents show:**
- The Seller calls these "ordinary course."
- The Disclosure Letter says the renewals are related and should be "read together for timing/scope." It does not say whether they are avoidable, terminable or accrued.
- Three equal related renewals suggest one AUD 330k commitment may have been split, possibly to stay under a contract-approval threshold in the conduct-of-business covenants. We should check this against our draft thresholds.

**Push back:**
- Ask for the contracts, timing and business rationale.
- Confirm whether the renewals are arm's-length, terminable and accrued.
- Aggregate related contracts in the conduct-of-business covenants.
- Treat any prepayment after the locked-box or accounts date as leakage or a debt-like item where appropriate.
- Require Buyer consent before any further Sandbar commitments.

### 15. Title evidence: share register only (DD-012)
**Analysis:** A company's own register is not sufficient title evidence on its own. The Disclosure Letter (item 10) itself notes the Buyer has not verified title.

**Push back:**
- We need to do our own checks: ASIC company search and share-structure check, PPSR search against the Seller and the Company, share certificates, and confirmation there are no options, convertibles or rights.
- The SPA needs a full title warranty, treated as fundamental (item 1).

### 16. Lower-priority items
- **Office lease (DD-007):** The lease needs only a notification. Ensure it is given, and confirm there is no change-of-control or default trigger elsewhere in the lease.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** The contract restricts assignment. Confirm it has no separate change-of-control clause, which a share sale would trip even though it is not an assignment.
- **Disclosure Letter 1.4 (non-admission):** Acceptable in principle, provided it does not dilute the specific indemnities.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer response | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | "[STANDARD]" labels / efficiency note | Clauses deemed agreed; review only [OPEN] | Reject; nothing agreed until confirmed in writing | High |
| 1 | Title/capacity warranties | 20% cap, 18 months | 100% of price; 6+ years; no thresholds | **Critical** |
| 2 | Scope of limitations / non-reliance | All Claims of any nature | General warranties only; carve out fraud, tax, indemnities, leakage | **Critical** |
| 7 | General disclosure | Whole data room plus public records | Specific, fair disclosure only; no bring-down cure | **Critical** |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge | Actual plus "discoverable" knowledge bars claims | Delete; fallback actual knowledge of named people | **Critical** |
| 10 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Release after Completion | Repay from price at Completion; releases delivered at Completion | **Critical** |
| 11 | Bluefen (30% of revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; any written consent suffices | Condition precedent; consent satisfactory to Buyer; walk right | **Critical** |
| 9 | Bonuses AUD 420k plus on-costs | Not in funds flow | Debt-like deduction plus indemnity | High |
| 13 | DD-006 privacy incident | "Not material" | Full information; covenants; uncapped specific indemnity; escrow | High |
| 12 | Ironquay SOW3 IP | Payment-only indemnity | Confirmatory assignment before Completion; broad indemnity | High |
| 6 | Recovery risk | None offered | Escrow/retention, guarantee or W&I | High |
| 3 | Cap and basket | 20%; excess-only basket | Tipping basket; higher cap if no W&I | Medium |
| 4/5 | Tax and IP time limits | 18 months; "settled" | Tax indemnity; 5–7 years | Medium |
| 14 | Sandbar AUD 330k | Ordinary course | Diligence; aggregate in covenants; leakage treatment | Medium |
| 15 | Title evidence | Share register only | Independent ASIC/PPSR checks plus fundamental warranty | Medium |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification / assignment only | Confirm there are no change-of-control triggers | Low |

**Overall:** The package has three features that together leave the Buyer with very little warranty protection:
- general disclosure of the whole data room;
- a Buyer-knowledge bar extending to anything "discoverable";
- limitations applying to all Claims, including title.

It also pushes about AUD 3.6m+ of known value leakage onto the Buyer: Riverlark AUD 3.2m, bonuses AUD 420k plus on-costs, and possibly Ironquay AUD 180k. On top of that, Bluefen and DD-006 are open risks.

I recommend we send a full mark-up rejecting the "pre-agreed" framing. Separately, we should ask for the Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and DD-006 supporting documents now, as the condition and indemnity drafting depends on them. Our tax and privacy specialists should confirm the on-cost and Notifiable Data Breaches points before the mark-up goes out.

- The Seller says the consent is "addressed", but the Disclosure Letter (item 2) says there is no final consent and no evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- "Reasonable endeavours", plus deemed satisfaction on delivery of *any* written consent, would let a consent with onerous conditions satisfy the condition. Examples would be repricing or a shortened term.

**Push back:**
- Make it a condition precedent: unconditional written consent from Bluefen, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer acting reasonably. All 11.3 conditions must be satisfied or be on terms the Buyer accepts.
- The Seller should use "all reasonable endeavours", with the Buyer involved in communications with Bluefen.
- The condition is waivable only by the Buyer, with a long-stop date and a termination right.
- Add a warranty that Bluefen has not indicated it will terminate, reduce or renegotiate.

### 12. Ironquay SOW3 IP (DD-004 / DD-010)
**What the documents show:**
- Clause 7.3 means the SOW3 Project Materials **do not transfer** until all SOW3 fees are paid.
- AUD 180,000 is recorded as open. There is no evidence of payment and no confirmatory assignment.
- The existing indemnity covers only the payment. It does not cover:
  - losing the IP;
  - third-party infringement claims;
  - redevelopment or replacement costs;
  - business interruption.

**Push back:**
- Before Completion, either pay Ironquay out, with the payment treated as a debt-like deduction if made by the Company, or obtain an executed **confirmatory assignment** from Ironquay. Make this a condition precedent or Completion deliverable.
- Broaden the specific indemnity to cover all loss from any failure of the Company to own the SOW3 materials. It should sit outside the general cap and thresholds and not be qualified by disclosure.

### 13. DD-006 export and privacy incident (about 1,240 records)
**What the documents show:**
- The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." The Disclosure Letter says scope, access and notification status are all unknown.
- The data includes names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps, which is personal information.
- Under the Privacy Act's Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity must reasonably and expeditiously assess a suspected eligible data breach, generally within 30 days of becoming aware.
- The incident predates 22 September 2026, so that period has likely passed. A failure to assess or notify may already be a compliance issue in its own right.
- Privacy penalties and regulator scrutiny have increased materially since the 2022 amendments.

**Push back:**
- Require immediate disclosure of:
  - the full incident file;
  - the date of awareness;
  - the steps taken;
  - any forensic report;
  - any OAIC or affected-individual notification.
- Add a pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment, make any required notifications and keep the Buyer informed.
- Add a **specific indemnity** for all loss from the incident (regulator penalties, claims, remediation and notification costs). It should sit outside the cap, basket and de minimis, not be qualified by disclosure, and be backed by escrow.
- Consider a condition or walk right if the investigation reveals a materially larger incident.

### 14. Sandbar supplier renewals, 3 × AUD 110,000 (DD-008 / DD-011)
**What the documents show:**
- The Seller calls these "ordinary course."
- The Disclosure Letter says the renewals are related and should be "read together for timing/scope." It does not say whether they are avoidable, terminable or accrued.
- Three equal related renewals suggest one AUD 330k commitment may have been split, possibly to stay under a contract-approval threshold in the conduct-of-business covenants. We should check this against our draft thresholds.

**Push back:**
- Ask for the contracts, timing and business rationale.
- Confirm whether the renewals are arm's-length, terminable and accrued.
- Aggregate related contracts in the conduct-of-business covenants.
- Treat any prepayment after the locked-box or accounts date as leakage or a debt-like item where appropriate.
- Require Buyer consent before any further Sandbar commitments.

### 15. Title evidence: share register only (DD-012)
**Analysis:** A company's own register is not sufficient title evidence on its own. The Disclosure Letter (item 10) itself notes the Buyer has not verified title.

**Push back:**
- We need to do our own checks: ASIC company search and share-structure check, PPSR search against the Seller and the Company, share certificates, and confirmation there are no options, convertibles or rights.
- The SPA needs a full title warranty, treated as fundamental (item 1).

### 16. Lower-priority items
- **Office lease (DD-007):** The lease needs only a notification. Ensure it is given, and confirm there is no change-of-control or default trigger elsewhere in the lease.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** The contract restricts assignment. Confirm it has no separate change-of-control clause, which a share sale would trip even though it is not an assignment.
- **Disclosure Letter 1.4 (non-admission):** Acceptable in principle, provided it does not dilute the specific indemnities.

**Overall:** The package has three features that together leave the Buyer with very little warranty protection:
- general disclosure of the whole data room;
- a Buyer-knowledge bar extending to anything "discoverable";
- limitations applying to all Claims, including title.

It also pushes about AUD 3.6m+ of known value leakage onto the Buyer: Riverlark AUD 3.2m, bonuses AUD 420k plus on-costs, and possibly Ironquay AUD 180k. On top of that, Bluefen and DD-006 are open risks.

I recommend we send a full mark-up rejecting the "pre-agreed" framing. Separately, we should ask for the Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and DD-006 supporting documents now, as the condition and indemnity drafting depends on them. Our tax and privacy specialists should confirm the on-cost and Notifiable Data Breaches points before the mark-up goes out.
